summary: The root عذر primarily means to excuse or free from blame. It can also mean to be faulty, deserving punishment, or to aid someone.
lane: 1 عَذَرَهُ ذ , aor. عَذِرَ , inf. n. عُذْرٌ (S, O, Msb, K) and عُذُرٌ (S, O, K) and عُذْرَى (O, K) and مَعْذِرَةٌ and مَعْذُرَةٌ (K) [all of which are also used as simple substs.]; and ; (S, O, Msb, K;) He excused him; freed, cleared, or exempted, him from blame; exculpated him: (Msb:) or he accepted his excuse: properly, عَذَرْتُ signifies I cancelled evil conduct. (TA.) [See also عُذْرٌ below.] You say, عَذَرْتُهُ فِيمَا صَنَعَ (S, O, Msb) I excused, or exculpated, him for what he did. (Msb.) And in a trad. of El-Mikdád it is said, لَقَدْ ٱللّٰهُ إِلَيْكَ i.e. Verily God hath excused thee, and exempted thee from the obligation to fight against the unbelievers; for he had become extremely fat, and unable to fight. (TA.) And you say [also], عَذَرَهُ عَنِ الشَّىْءِ He excused him for, or from, the thing. (MA.) [And accord. to Golius, عَذَرَهُ عَلَى الشَّىْءِ , as well as فِى الشَّىْءِ : but he has not mentioned his authority: see an explanation of عَذِيرٌ , from which the former phrase was perhaps derived by him.] And عَذَرْتُهُ مِنْ فُلَانٍ [ I excused him, or held him excusable, for his conduct to such a one ]; meaning, I did not blame him, but I blamed such a one. (S, * TA.) And مَنْ يَعْذِرُنِى مِنْهُ Who will excuse me, or make my excuse, if I requite him (Msb, TA) for his action, (Msb,) or for his evil action, (TA,) and will not blame me (Msb, TA) for it? (Msb:) or who will excuse me with respect to his case, and will not blame me for it? (Msb.) [And a similar ex. is mentioned in the TA with فِى in the place of مِنْ .] -b2- [Hence,] عَذَرَ , (Az, S, IKtt, O, Msb, K,) aor. عَذِرَ ; (O, TA;) and , (S, IKtt, Msb, K,) inf. n. إِعْذَارٌ ; (TA;) He was vitious, or faulty, and corrupt: (Msb:) or he was guilty of many crimes, sins, faults, offences, or acts of disobedience, (S, O, Msb, K,) so as to vender him excusable who punished him. (TA.) It is said in a trad., لَنْ يَهْلِكَ النَّاسُ حَتَّى يَعْذِرُوا مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ , (O, and so in some copies of the S and K,) or , (so in other copies of the S and K, ) both of which readings are the same in meaning, (TA,) i. e. [ Men will not perish, or die, ] until they are guilty of many crimes, or sins, &c.; (S, O, Msb, K;) meaning, (accord. to A 'Obeyd, S, O,) until they deserve punishment, so as to render excusable him who punishes them. (S, A, O, TA.) And you say, مِنْ نَفْسِهِ , meaning He placed himself within the power of another. (TA.) -A2- And عَذَرْتُهُ I aided him, or assisted him, against an enemy. (Msb.) -A3- عَذَرَ , inf. n. عَذْرٌ , He cut, or cut off. (TA: but only the inf. n. of the verb in this sense is there mentioned.) -b2- And [hence, probably, as is implied in a passage in the TA, (see عُذْرَةٌ ,)] عَذَرَ , aor. عَذِرَ , (S, O, * Msb, K) inf. n. عَذْرٌ ; (S, Msb;) and ; (S, O, Msb, K;) both as expl. by A 'Obeyd; (S;) (tropical:) He circumcised a boy, (S, O, Msb, K,) and in like manner a girl; (S, O, Msb;) but when a girl is the object, خَفَضَ is more common. (S, O.) -A4- عَذَرَ الفَرَسَ بِالعِذَارِ , aor. عَذِرَ and عَذُرَ ; and ; He fastened, or bound, the horse's عِذَار [q. v.]: (S, O, K:) and الفَرَسَ he bridled the horse; syn. أَلْجَمَهُ ; (K, TA;) as also عَذَرَهُ , and : (TA:) or , (K,) or , (thus in the TA,) he put to him [or upon him ] an عِذَار ; (K, TA;) and so عَذَرَهُ , aor. عَذِرَ and عَذُرَ , inf. n. عَذْرٌ : (Msb:) and اللِّجَامَ he put to the لجام [i. e. bridle or bit ] an عِذَار . (TA.) -b2- And it is said in the Tahdheeb of IKtt that عَذَرْتُ الفَرَسَ , inf. n. عَذْرٌ , signifies I cauterized the horse in the place of the عِذَار : -b3- and also حملت على عذاره [an explanation in which there seems to be a mistranscription or an omission, or both; perhaps correctly جَعَلْتُ عَلَى الفَرَسِ عِذَارَهُ I put upon the horse his عذار ; a meaning given above]; and is a dial. var. thereof. (TA.) -b4- عُذِرَ said of a camel means He was branded with the mark called عِذَار . (TA.) -b5- [Hence, app., the phrase عَذَرَهُ بِاللَّوْمِ (assumed tropical:) He branded him with blame; like خَطَمَهُ باللوم , q.v.] -A5- عَذَرَهُ , from العُذْرَةُ , He (God, S) caused him (i. e. a child, TA) to be affected with the pain, in the fauces, termed عُذْرَة : and عُذِرَ He was, or became, affected therewith: (S, K, * TA:) inf. n. عَذْرٌ and عُذْرَةٌ . (IKtt, TA.)

headwords.def: aor. عَ ِرَ, inf. n. عُ ْرٌ (S, O, Msb, K) and عُ ُرٌ (S, O, K) and عُ ْرَى (O, K) and مَعْ ِرَةٌ and مَعْ ُرَةٌ (K) [all of which are also used as simple substs.]; and; (S, O, Msb, K;) He excused him; freed, cleared, or exempted, him from blame; exculpated him: (Msb:) or he accepted his excuse: properly, عَ َرْتُ signifies I cancelled evil conduct. (TA.) [See also عُ ْرٌ below.] You say, عَ َرْتُهُ فِيمَا صَنَعَ (S, O, Msb) I excused, or exculpated, him for what he did.

inf. n. تَعْ ِيرٌ, He was without excuse; (K, * TA;) as also, (K, TA,) inf. n. مُعَا َرَةٌ: (TA:) he affected to excuse himself, but had no excuse: he excused himself, but did not adduce an excuse [ that was valid ].
عَاْ َرَ see 2, first sentence. [And see also the last clause of the last paragraph of this art.]

: see 1, in five places from the commencement. Also He had an excuse; [or he was, or became, excusable; ] (S, O, K;) and so. (S, O, K.) It is said in a prov., أَعْ َرَ مَنْ أَنْ َرَ [ He has an excuse, or is excusable, who warns ]. (S. [See also below: and see art. ن ر.

: see 8, in three places. Also He went backwards; drew back; remained behind; or held back: (K:) or he held back, or withheld himself, for a cause rendering him excused. (TA voce تَغَدَّرَ, q. v.) And He fled. (K.) You say, تع ّروا عَلَيْهِ They fled from him, and abstained from aiding, or assisting, him, or held back from him.

(S, O, Msb, &c.,) inf. n. اِعْتِ َارٌ, (S, O, TA,) and [quasi-inf. ns.] and; (TA;) and for اعت ر one says also اِعَ َّرَ, aor. يَعَ ِّرُ, inf. n. اِعِ َّارٌ; and it is allowable to say اِعِ ِّرَ, aor.

استع ر مِنْ فُلَانٍ He asked, or desired, to be excused if he should lay violent hands upon such a one [or requite him for an evil action ]; he said, مَنْ عَ ِيرِى مِنْ فُلَانٍ. (A, TA.) It is said in a trad. of the Prophet, اِسْتَعْ َرَ أَبَا بَكْرٍ مِنْ عَائِشَةَ i. e. He said to Aboo-Bekr, Undertake thou to excuse me for my conduct to 'Áïsheh if I discipline her, or chastise her.

(Msb, K) and (Msb) and (S, O, K) and (S, Msb) and (S, O, Msb, K) and and (K) [all as simple substs., but all except the third and the last mentioned also as inf. ns.,] An excuse; an apology; a plea whereby one excuses himself [or another ]: accord. to the B, عُ ْرٌ [as a subst.

[an epithet of which I find only the fem., with ة, mentioned]. دَارٌ عَ ِرَةٌ means A house, or dwelling, of which there are many traces, or relics. (O.) And أَرْضٌ عَ ِرَةٌ Land that does not yield herbage freely, and if it give growth to anything, this soon becomes blighted. (O and TA in art. عثر.)
: see عُ ْرٌ, in three places. Also pl. of عِ َارٌ [q. v.]. (S, O, Msb, K.)

The virginity, maidenhead, or hymen; syn. بَكَارَةٌ, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) or قِضَّةٌ; so called from عَ ْرٌ signifying the “ act of cutting, ” because a girl's hymen ( خَاتَمُ عُ ْرَتِهَا ) is rent when she is devirginated; (Lh, Az, TA;) العُ ْرَةُ being that whereby a girl is a virgin: (Lh, TA:) [and perhaps signifies the same: (see an ex. voce أَرِيمٌ; and see also the next sentence here following:)] pl. عُ َرٌ.
: see عُ ْرٌ, in two places: and see also 8. [Accord. to analogy, it signifies A mode, or manner, of excusing. ]

Human dung or ordure; (S, * O, * Msb, K, TA;) as also (IAar, IDrd, O, L, K, TA) and: (O, K:) pl. of the first [which is the most common] عَ ِرَاتٌ, (Msb,) and of ↓ the second عُ َرٌ. (IAar, TA.) And hence, (S, O, Msb,) (tropical:) The court, or yard, ( فِنَآء,) of a house: (S, O, Msb, K, TA:) so called because the human ordure ( العَ ِرَة ) used to be cast in it: (S, O, Msb:) or, accord.
: see عُ ْرٌ, in two places.

A virgin: (S, O, K:) used as an epithet: you say جَارِيَةٌ عَ ْرَآءُ a virgin girl: (TA:) and اِمْرَأَةٌ عَ ْرَآءُ, meaning َاتُ عَ ْرَةٍ: (Msb:) accord. to IAar alone, so called لِضِيقِهَا, from تَعَ َّرَ عَلَيْهِ الأَمْرُ: (TA:) pl. عَ َارَى and عَ َارٍ [with the art. العَ َارِى, and thus written in the S and O and K] (S, O, K, TA) and عَ ْرَاوَاتٌ, (S, O, K,) like صَحَارَى [&c.].

A certain appertenance of a horse or the like; (S, O;) i. e. the part, (T, M, Mgh,) or strap, (Msb,) of the bridle, (T, M, Mgh, Msb,) that lies, (T,) or extends down, (M, K,) upon the cheek, (M, Mgh, Msb, K,) or two cheeks, (T,) of the horse (T, M, Mgh, Msb, K) or the like: (T, Mgh, Msb:) the عَ َارَانِ are the two straps upon the two cheeks of the horse, on the right and left: (IDrd in his Book on the Saddle and Bridle:) or, as some say, the عِ َار is the two straps of the bridle…

: see عُ ْرٌ, in two places. Also i. q. [act. part. n. of 1, Excusing; an excuser; &c.]. (K.) You say, مَنْ عَ ِيرِى مِنْ فُلَانٍ Who will excuse me, or make my excuse, or be my excuser, if I requite such a one (Msb, TA) for his action, (Msb,) or for his evil action, (TA,) and will not blame me (Msb, TA) for it? or who will excuse me with respect to the case of such a one, and not blame me for it? (Msb: [see عَ َرْتُهُ مِنْ فُلَانٍ: and see also 10:]) or who will aid me, or assist me,…

[ A disposition to excuse ]. One says, مَا عِنْدَهُمْ عَ ِيرَةٌ, meaning [ They have not a disposition to excuse; or] they do not excuse. (O.) [See also غَفِيرَةٌ.] See also عَا ِرٌ: and إِعْ َارٌ. Also I. q. عَدِيرَةٌ [app. as syn. with رَغِيدَةٌ ]. (O, TA.)

(tropical:) Evil in disposition; (S, O, K, TA, and Ham p. 417;) as though needing to excuse himself for his evildoing; (Ham ibid.;) vehement in commanding and forbidding, (Ham p. 469,) and in spirit. (K.) [ Clamorous. (Freytag, from the Deewán of Jereer.)] Applied to an ass, Wide in the جَوْف [i. e. belly, or chest ], (S, O, K,) and فَحَّاش [app. meaning very lewd ].

: see عَ ِيرٌ; and عُ ْرٌ, latter half. عَا ِرَةٌ, [fem. of عَا ِرٌ,] as an epithet applied to a woman: see the fem. of مَعْ ُورٌ. Also A scar, or mark of a wound; (S, O, K;) and so, (O, and thus in copies of the S,) or. (TA, and so in a copy of the S.) One says, تَرَكَ بِهِ عَا ِرًا He, or it, left upon him a scar, or mark of a wound. (TA.) And the same is said of rain, meaning, It left upon him, or it, a mark. (TA.) See also عَ ِرَةٌ, in two places.
as a subst.: see عَ ِرَةٌ.

A brand, or mark made with a hot iron, like a line: pl. عَوَا ِيرُ. (S, O.) And لَقِيتُ مِنْهُ عَا ُورًا is a saying mentioned by As, as meaning I experienced, from him, or it, evil: عَا ُورٌ being a dial. var. of عَاثُورٌ, or an instance of mispronunciation. (S, O.) العَا ُورُ also signifies What is cut off from the place of circumcision of a girl [which place is termed her عُ ْرَة ]. (O, TA.) See also عُ ْرَةٌ, last quarter.
: see عُ ْرَةٌ, last quarter.

(AZ, S, A, O, Msb, K,) originally an inf. n., (S, O, Msb,) and (S, A, O, K) and (A, K) and, (K,) A repast, or food, prepared on the occasion of a circumcision; (AZ, S, A, O, Msb, K;) or on some joyful occasion: (Msb:) and the last of these words likewise signifies a repast, or food, prepared on the occasion [ of the completion ] of a building: and also a repast, or food, which one prepares, and to which he invites his brethren, on the occasion of the acquisition of something new:…
; pl. مَعَا ِرُ: see عَ ِرَةٌ, second sentence.
: see مُعْتَ ِرٌ, in two places.
and مَعْ ُرَةٌ and مَعْ َرَةٌ; and the pl. مَعَا ِرُ: see عُ ْرٌ, in five places: and for the first, see also 8.
[properly signifying The place of the عِ َار or of the عِ َارَانِ ]: see عِ َارٌ, in four places.
and مُعِ ِّرٌ and مُعُ ِّرٌ: see مُعْتَ ِرٌ, in six places.

sing. of مَعَا ِيرُ, (O, K,) which signifies [ Excuses, or apologies; ] pleas, allegations, or arguments: (K, TA: see عُ ْرٌ, in two places:) and also, (K, TA,) in the dial. of El-Yemen, (TA,) Veils, curtains, or coverings. (O, K, TA.) The saying in the Kur [lxxv. 14 and 15], بَلِ ٱلْإِنْسَانُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ بَصِيرَةٌ وَلَوْ أَلْقَى مَعَا ِيرَهُ is expl.

Excused; freed, cleared, or exempted, from blame; exculpated. (Msb.) And [hence, perhaps,] مَعْ ُورَةٌ applied to a woman signifies مُسْتَحَاضَةٌ [q. v. in art. حيض ]: and sometimes one says; as meaning having an excuse: (Msb:) the latter is said to be used in the sense of مُسْتَحَاضَةٌ; but it requires consideration; (O, TA;) as though it were of the measure فَاعِلَةٌ in the sense of مَفْعُولَةٌ, [i. e. in the sense of مَعْ ُورَةٌ as meaning excused, ] from إِقَامَةُ العُ ْرِ.
: see its pl. in the last clause of the following paragraph.

One excusing himself, whether he have, or have not, an excuse: (TA:) the person to whom this epithet is applied may be a speaker of truth, and he may be not a speaker of truth: (Msb, TA:) and so, which, as applied to a speaker of truth, signifies having an excuse, like مُعْتَ ِرٌ, (S, O, K,) [of which it is a variation,] for the ت is changed into , and this is incorporated [into the radical ], and its vowel is transferred to the ع, like as is the case in يَخَصِّمُونَ; (S, O;)…

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
